newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul stocks seen rising, led by export industries.
newsitem.headline: Seoul stocks seen rising, led by export industries.

text.p: Stocks are expected to rise on Monday led by brisk buying in shares of shipbuilding, steelmaking and other major export industries, brokers said.
They said the Japanese yen's recent gains versus the U.S. dollar would remain the biggest factor keeping investors' sentiment buoyant.
"Shipbuilders, steel makers and synthetic textile makers are forecast to lead gains today," said Ahn Jong-sun of Coryo Securities.
The composite index closed Saturday's half-day session up 6.72 points at 706.25.
Brokers said the market's overall sentiment would also be boosted by the belief that the bribery scandal involving president Kim Young-sam's son had passed the critical point.
Kim Hyun-chul, the second son of the president, was arrested for taking bribes and evading tax on money he took as gifts.
"For investors, the arrest meant a major negative factor has now disappeared," said Ahn.
